question: What obligations apply to providers of high-risk AI systems?
answer:
Providers of high-risk AI systems have several obligations under the EU AI Act, including:

1. Ensuring compliance with the requirements set out in Section 2 (Article 16, point (a)).
2. Indicating their name, registered trade name or trademark, and contact address on the AI system, its packaging, or accompanying documentation (Article 16, point (b)).
3. Having a quality management system in place that complies with Article 17 (Article 16, point (c)).
4. Keeping the documentation referred to in Article 18 (Article 16, point (d)).
5. Keeping the logs automatically generated by their high-risk AI systems as referred to in Article 19 (Article 16, point (e)).
6. Ensuring the high-risk AI system undergoes the relevant conformity assessment procedure as referred to in Article 43 before being placed on the market or put into service (Article 16, point (f)).
7. Affixing the CE marking to the high-risk AI system or its packaging or accompanying documentation to indicate conformity with the Regulation, in accordance with Article 48 (Article 16, point (h)).
8. Complying with the registration obligations referred to in Article 49(1) (Article 16, point (i)).
9. Upon a reasoned request of a national competent authority, demonstrating the conformity of the high-risk AI system with the requirements set out in Section 2 (Article 16, point (k)).
10. Ensuring the high-risk AI system complies with accessibility requirements in accordance with Directives (EU) 2016/2102 and (EU) 2019/882 (Article 16, point (l)).
